questions.q: Who came out of Judah by the word of Yahweh?
questions.a: A man of God came out of Judah by the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did the man of God cry out against the altar at Bethel?
questions.a: The man of God cried out against the altar, “On you they will burn men’s bones.”

questions.q: What sign did the man of God give about the altar?
questions.a: The man of God gave a sign saying, “The altar will be split apart and the ashes on it will be poured out.”

questions.q: What happened to Jeroboam’s hand when he reached out from the altar?
questions.a: When Jeroboam reached out from the altar, his hand was dried up so he could not draw it back to himself.

questions.q: What happened to the altar?
questions.a: The altar was split apart and the ashes poured out, just as the man of God described.

questions.q: What happened when the man of God prayed to Yahweh about Jeroboam’s hand?
questions.a: When the man of God prayed to Yahweh, the king’s hand was restored and became as it was before.

questions.q: What did the king say to the man of God?
questions.a: The king said to the man of God, “Come home with me, and I will give you a reward.”

questions.q: What did the man of God say to the king?
questions.a: The man of God said to the king, “I will not go with you.”

questions.q: What did the man of God do after speaking with the king?
questions.a: After speaking with the king, the man of God returned home by a different way than he came to Bethel.

questions.q: Where did an old prophet live?
questions.a: An old prophet lived in Bethel.

questions.q: Who saw the way that the man of God had gone from Bethel?
questions.a: The old prophet’s sons saw the way that the man of God walked who had come from Judah.

questions.q: Where did the old prophet find the man of God?
questions.a: The old prophet found the man of God sitting under the oak tree.

questions.q: What did the old prophet say to the man of God?
questions.a: The old prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat food.”

questions.q: What was the man of God’s answer to the old prophet?
questions.a: The man of God answered, “I am not allowed to go with you into your house, or to eat or drink anything with you.”

questions.q: What was the old prophet’s answer to the man of God?
questions.a: The old prophet was lying to the man of God when he told him that an angel told the old prophet to bring him back to your house.

questions.q: Where did the man of God go after the old prophet lied to him?
questions.a: The man of God went back and ate food and drank water in his house.

questions.q: What came to the old prophet as they sat at the table?
questions.a: The word of Yahweh came to the old prophet as they sat at the table.

questions.q: What did the word of Yahweh say to the man of God?
questions.a: The word of Yahweh said, “Because you came back and ate food and drank water, your body will not be buried in the tomb of your fathers.”

questions.q: What did the old prophet do after they ate?
questions.a: After they ate, the old prophet saddled the man of God’s donkey for him.

questions.q: What happened after the man of God had gone?
questions.a: After the man of God had gone, a lion met him on the road and killed him.

questions.q: What did men do when they saw the body of the man of God lying on the road?
questions.a: When men saw the man of God’s body lying on the road, they came back and told it in the city of the old prophet.

questions.q: What was the old prophet’s answer to the men?
questions.a: The old prophet answered that this was the man of God who had disobeyed the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did the old prophet do after hearing the men?
questions.a: The old prophet spoke to his sons to saddle his donkey, and he went and found the body left in the road.

questions.q: What did the old prophet do with the body of the man of God?
questions.a: The old prophet took up the body of the man of God and buried him in his own grave.

questions.q: What did the old prophet say to his sons about his own burial?
questions.a: The old prophet said to his sons, “When I am dead, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried.”

questions.q: What thing became sin to the family of Jeroboam and caused it to be cut off from the face of the earth?
questions.a: Jeroboam did not turn away from evil, and even more, he consecrated as priests anyone who wanted to be a priest.

commentary.text: The disobedient prophet is slain, Jeroboam's obstinacy.

Verses 1–10 In threatening the altar, the prophet threatens the founder and worshippers. Idolatrous worship will not continue, but the word of the Lord will endure for ever. The prediction plainly declared that the family of David would continue, and support true religion, when the ten tribes would not be able to resist them. If God, in justice, harden the hearts of sinners, so that the hand they have stretched out in sin they cannot pull in again by repentance, that is a spiritual judgment, represented by this, and much more dreadful. Jeroboam looked for help, not from his calves, but from God only, from his power, and his favour. The time may come when those that hate the preaching, would be glad of the prayers of faithful ministers. Jeroboam does not desire the prophet to pray that his sin might be pardoned, and his heart changed, but only that his hand might be restored. He seemed affected for the present with both the judgment and the mercy, but the impression wore off. God forbade his messenger to eat or drink in Bethel, to show his detestation of their idolatry and apostacy from God, and to teach us not to have fellowship with the works of darkness. Those have not learned self-denial, who cannot forbear one forbidden meal.

The old prophet's conduct proves that he was not really a godly man. When the change took place under Jeroboam, he preferred his ease and interest to his religion. He took a very bad method to bring the good prophet back. It was all a lie. Believers are most in danger of being drawn from their duty by plausible pretences of holiness. We may wonder that the wicked prophet went unpunished, while the holy man of God was suddenly and severely punished. What shall we make of this? The judgments of God are beyond our power to fathom; and there is a judgment to come. Nothing can excuse any act of wilful disobedience. This shows what they must expect who hearken to the great deceiver. They that yield to him as a tempter, will be terrified by him as a tormentor. Those whom he now fawns upon, he will afterwards fly upon; and whom he draws into sin, he will try to drive to despair.

God is displeased at the sins of his own people; and no man shall be protected in disobedience, by his office, his nearness to God, or any services he has done for him. God warns all whom he employs, strictly to observe their orders. We cannot judge of men by their sufferings, nor of sins by present punishments; with some, the flesh is destroyed, that the spirit may be saved; with others, the flesh is pampered, that the soul may ripen for hell. Jeroboam returned not from his evil way. He promised himself that the calves would secure the crown to his family, but they lost it, and sunk his family. Those betray themselves who think to support themselves by any sin whatever. Let us dread prospering in sinful ways; pray to be kept from every delusion and temptation, and to be enabled to walk with self-denying perseverance in the way of God's commands.
